_note: FIRST DRAFTED ARTIFACT. Fills the D and E gaps the Phase 1 mine left on boiler, which the placement pass named the priority. Every item carries a convergence class and an anchor; single-source items carry a stated reason or they are cut before this sheet reaches a sitting.
subject: BOILER
source_master: DRAFTED — no master. Phase 1's CSP corpus carries no safety-device tests and no readings table; that absence is what this fills.

_anchors.CSA B149.1: Natural Gas and Propane Installation Code — Ontario installation requirements for gas-fired appliances
_anchors.TSSA: Technical Standards and Safety Authority — Ontario AHJ for fuel-burning appliances
_anchors.manufacturer IOM: the standing line item; per-manufacturer sequences never enter a template

items.label: High-limit control tripped and proven to shut down the burner (manual reset verified)
items.note: A high limit is a manual-reset device by design; proving the trip without proving the reset leaves half the device untested.

items.label: Operating limit tripped and proven to cycle the burner
items.note: Distinct from the high limit: the operating control cycles, the high limit locks out.

items.label: Low-water cutoff proven — burner locks out on simulated low water
items.note: Required at installation on boilers above radiation level or where the AHJ requires it.

items.label: Flame failure proven — main fuel valve closes on loss of flame signal; closure time recorded
items.note: Loss of flame must close the safety shutoff valves immediately; the time is the evidence, so it is also an E row.

items.label: High gas pressure switch tripped and proven
items.note: Gas-fired only — a conditional section per the ruled variant principle, not a template fork.

items.label: Low gas pressure switch tripped and proven
Blocked vent / air-proving switch tripped; burner lockout confirmed
Relief valve rating verified against MAWP; seal intact and discharge unobstructed
Emergency fuel shutoff at the room exit operated; fuel and power both drop
items.convergence_reason: ONTARIO CODE REQUIREMENT — TSSA requires a remote emergency shutoff for fuel-fired appliance rooms. No national source in the anchor set carries it, so it is kept on a stated jurisdictional basis rather than cut.

items.label: Freezestat trip proven (where a coil is exposed to outdoor air)
items.note: NAMED BY THE OWNER while ruling the residue: the missing half of 'Coil Protected From Freezing', which records the provisions and never proves the trip.

items.label: Firing rate at each recorded point (%)
Flame-failure valve closure time (s)
items.note: The measured half of the D row above — the trip is proven there, the number is recorded here.

_cut_before_the_sitting.label: Burner nozzle part number recorded
_cut_before_the_sitting.why_cut: Single-source with no jurisdictional basis, and per-manufacturer detail — it belongs in the IOM attachment, not the template. The template holds consensus, not collection.

_cut_before_the_sitting.label: Refractory dry-out schedule followed
_cut_before_the_sitting.why_cut: Applies to one boiler construction only; no convergence and no code basis in the anchor set.

_ratification_note: Ratified as drafted, no amendments. 13 universal / 8 type-common / 1 single-source; the TSSA item survives on the stated-reason standard; both pre-sitting cuts endorsed.
